title: State: let the current state answer
summary: A vending machine hands each event to its current state object. Idle accepts a coin and switches to Paid; Paid dispenses and switches back. The machine never checks a status flag.
code: # Each state answers the events and picks the next state; the machine never checks a flag.
triggers: the same call behaves differently depending on the object's current mode, with rules for which mode comes next
status flags checked by if/elif in every method: vending machines, order lifecycles, traffic lights
prompts: A turnstile ignores pushes until a ticket is scanned, lets exactly one person through, then locks again. Extra scans while it's unlocked must not bank extra passes.
A document moves from draft to review to published. Editing is allowed only in draft, approving only in review, and each step decides where the document goes next.
invariant: The machine always holds exactly one state object; each event is answered by that state, and only states change machine.state.
mantra: Ask the state; the state picks the next state.
pitfalls: Assign machine.state, not self.state: the state is handed the machine so it can switch it.
Every state answers every event, even if only to refuse it.
If the caller picks the object and it never replaces itself, that's Strategy.
